absent: Adapter lock operation implementations, blocking context and nesting rules between root and segment scopes.
I2C algorithm functionality bit definitions, quirk flag meanings and client address validation.
Enabled firmware-node, device-tree and ACPI lookup and device creation behavior.
Common ICMPv6 sender behavior, neighbor-discovery offload path and drop-reason handling.

findings.text: I2C bus access is mediated through per-adapter lock operations selected at call time. Lock, conditional lock and unlock helpers forward caller supplied scope flags to the adapter current handler and propagate its outcome where applicable. Two scope selectors exist, one for the root adapter and one for a segment, occupying distinct low-order bit positions.

Adapter suspend state is a single flag inside a protected word. Marking suspended acquires root scope, asserts the flag, then releases; marking resumed acquires the same scope, clears the flag, then releases. The flag therefore only transitions while the root lock is held.

Capability discovery queries the adapter algorithm handler for a bitmask and tests whether all requested bits are present. Quirk discovery reports false when no quirk descriptor is attached, otherwise tests whether all requested quirk bits are present. Adapter numeric identity is exposed directly from its stored number.

Message address helpers derive wire octets from stored address plus direction indication. The short form shifts the address left by one and merges the read indication. The extended ten-bit form produces a high octet carrying a fixed marker pattern plus the two high address bits and the read indication, and a low octet carrying the remaining eight address bits.

Driver enrolment is provided by a registration macro plus module and built-in wrappers that bind add and remove handlers. A client helper reports whether a client object is usable and has an attached driver, treating null and error-encoded pointers as driverless.

When firmware and bus lookup support is unavailable the fragments define neutral fallbacks. Firmware-node device, adapter and referenced-adapter lookups yield null; device-tree device and adapter lookups and referenced-adapter retrieval likewise yield null while board-info extraction reports unsupported; resource extraction reports absent, client counting and bus-speed discovery yield zero, creation by firmware node reports missing device, adapter lookup by handle yields null, and probe-waive checks report false.

When device-tree support is present, device and adapter lookups convert the supplied device-tree node into a firmware-node handle in a null-safe manner and delegate to the corresponding firmware-node lookup. The conversion yields null for a null node and otherwise the embedded handle; a disabled configuration always yields null. Device-based creation resolves its firmware node with const-correct dispatch and delegates to creation by firmware node.
Interval timer interface uses port sixty-seven for mode, sixty-four for channel zero and sixty-six for channel two. The latch value is defined as tick rate rounded to whole ticks per timer interrupt.

Hardware-monitoring class occupies the lowest class bit and a deprecated class occupies bit eight. The address-list terminator value is sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-four. Address-list construction builds a read-only array of supplied addresses followed by that terminator.

Control message header access interprets the packet transport offset as the header location. The transport pointer is computed from packet head plus stored offset, with a one-time debug check that the offset was previously established by comparing against an all-ones sentinel.

Enabled builds forward sends to a common sender, either reusing the packet stored control block or a zeroed parameter block for offload. Disabled builds provide empty operations with identical signatures. Parameter-problem reporting forwards code and position with a default drop reason. Error classification returns true for destination unreachable, packet too big, time exceeded and parameter problem types, otherwise false.

Printable hardware-address length equals three times hardware address length minus one. Tag encapsulation adds four bytes; combined header length is eighteen and minimum frame size without checksum is sixty-four. Maximum payload is fifteen hundred, maximum frame without checksum is fifteen eighteen, and at most eight nested tags are parsed.

Tag control carries priority in the top three bits with shift thirteen, a format and eligibility indicator in bit twelve, and identifier in the low twelve bits. The identifier space size is four thousand ninety-six.

Virtual-function statistics record holds eight wide counters covering receive and transmit packets and bytes plus broadcast, multicast and dropped directions. Virtual-function info record holds numeric index, thirty-two byte hardware address area, virtual LAN identifier and quality, spoof-check, link state, rate bounds, query and trust flags, and big-endian VLAN protocol field.

Wire tag header holds two big-endian sixteen-bit fields for control information and encapsulated protocol. Tagged Ethernet header groups destination and source hardware addresses, then carries VLAN protocol, control information and encapsulated protocol as big-endian sixteen-bit fields.

Per-CPU statistics hold packet, byte and multicast counters in both directions with a synchronization object plus scalar receive-error and transmit-drop counts. Priority mapping nodes hold a socket priority, a quality value, a next pointer protected for deferred reclamation, and a reclamation callback head.

Device private state records ingress mapping count and eight-entry ingress table, egress mapping count and sixteen-entry table of mapping heads, protocol and identifier and flags, backing real device pointer with lifetime tracker and cached hardware address, plus directory entry and per-CPU statistics area and optional poll controller state.

Tagged header accessors interpret either the packet media-header offset or the packet data pointer as the tagged header. Tag state is held in combined packet fields; presence tests the combined validity word, retrieval returns the stored control value, and identifier, indicator and priority extractions mask and shift that value per the tag layout.

Reception-filter information management for customer and service tags must run with routing-table lock held, asserted at entry. Retrieval operations emit a push notification and convert notifier outcome to error status; release operations emit a drop notification without status.

Egress quality mapping lookup executes under read-side critical section. It selects a bucket by the low four bits of socket priority, walks the chain following deferred-reclamation pointers, and on priority match captures the quality value with a single-load accessor before exiting; absence yields zero. Tables live in device private state reachable from the device object.

Enabled builds identify tagged devices by testing a private flag and expose private state as the device private area. Disabled builds report no device as tagged, deep lookup yields null, and iteration yields success without invoking the action.

Disabled configuration provides neutral shims: real-device, identifier and protocol accessors warn once and return null or zero; egress-mask, receive handling, identifier addition, bulk addition by device and usage tests return zero or false; removals perform no action.

Tagged ethertype test accepts only the two standard tagged values after byte-order conversion. Hardware offload capability is true only when protocol and feature pair match: customer tag with customer-tag transmit feature, or service tag with service-tag transmit feature.

Inner tag insertion validates that the requested media length is linearly available, ensures headroom for tag plus metadata, grows the packet start, relocates media bytes, adjusts the media offset when set, and populates protocol and control fields according to whether the original protocol area is already present. Short-tag path fixes media length to Ethernet header size. Failures report invalid argument for unavailable length and out-of-memory for head-expansion failure.

Linearity probing first allows reallocation, succeeds immediately when already linear, rejects lengths beyond total length as too small, and otherwise attempts to extend the linear area reporting out-of-memory on failure. Copy-on-write handling computes head shortfall and expands the head with atomic allocation and padding when short or when the header is shared. Shared-header detection inspects clone state and shared-info reference counts excluding the current reference.

Post-push relocation moves both metadata and payload by a signed displacement, clearing metadata when layout checks fail. Metadata end is defined as the media header, clearing sets length to zero, and length is stored in shared packet info. Headroom is the distance between data and head pointers.

Tag-insertion wrappers free the packet and yield null on inner-insertion failure, otherwise return the packet; one variant also installs the supplied protocol as the packet protocol. Accelerated-tag state is cleared by zeroing the combined tag word and copied by assigning that word between packets. Plain header access interprets packet data as the header; inner access interprets the inner media offset from packet head.

Packet-path entry points for software tagging accept a packet, protocol, control value and media length, attempt in-place insertion, and on success return the packet for continued transmission processing.
Header inclusion guards define unique macros to prevent multiple inclusion across translation units.
